title: Heat and Mass Transfer
description: Develop the ability to model, analyze, and design systems involving conductive, convective, radiative, diffusive, interphase, and simultaneous heat and mass transfer.

topics.title: Conduction
topics.description: Conduction is the baseline mechanism for heat diffusion through solids and stationary fluids. Students learn how material properties, geometry, and boundary conditions determine heat flow.

children.title: Fourier's law
children.description: Students learn the constitutive law for conductive heat flux.

children.title: Temperature gradient and heat flux direction
Thermal resistance
children.description: Students simplify conduction problems using circuit analogies.

children.title: Heat generation
children.description: Students analyze systems where heat is produced internally.

children.title: Boundary conditions
children.description: Students learn how physical surroundings enter conduction models.

topics.title: Steady and Transient Conduction
topics.description: This section separates equilibrium conduction from time-dependent thermal response. The point is to predict both final temperatures and how long systems take to heat or cool.

children.title: Steady-state conduction
children.description: Students solve temperature fields that no longer change with time.

children.title: Transient lumped analysis
children.description: Students learn when an object can be approximated as spatially uniform.

children.title: Transient distributed analysis
children.description: Students handle cases with internal temperature gradients.

children.title: Numerical conduction methods
children.description: Students get a practical bridge to computational heat transfer.

topics.title: Convection Fundamentals
topics.description: Convection couples heat transfer with fluid flow. Students learn why a heat-transfer coefficient is not just a property, but a result of geometry, flow, and thermal boundary layers.

children.title: Boundary-layer ideas
children.description: Students connect flow near surfaces to heat transfer.

children.title: Newton's law of cooling
children.description: Students learn the engineering model for convective heat flux.

children.title: Dimensionless groups
children.description: Students use nondimensional numbers to generalize data and correlations.

children.title: Energy balance links
children.description: Students connect surface convection to control-volume analysis.

topics.title: Forced and Natural Convection
topics.description: Forced and natural convection are taught together because both use correlations, but their driving mechanisms differ. Students learn how pumps, fans, wind, and buoyancy change heat-transfer behavior.

children.title: External forced convection
children.description: Students analyze flow over plates, cylinders, and bodies.

children.title: Internal forced convection
children.description: Students analyze flow through pipes, tubes, and ducts.

children.title: Constant wall temperature versus heat flux
Natural convection
children.description: Students learn buoyancy-driven heat transfer.

children.title: Phase-change convection
children.description: Students get essential exposure to boiling and condensation.

topics.title: Radiation
topics.description: Radiation matters whenever temperatures are high, surfaces exchange across space, or vacuum/gas paths limit conduction and convection. Students learn radiative exchange from surface physics to enclosure calculations.

children.title: Radiation fundamentals
children.description: Students learn the basic laws of thermal radiation.

children.title: Surface properties
children.description: Students connect material finish and wavelength to radiation exchange.

children.title: View factors
children.description: Students learn geometric weighting of radiation exchange.

children.title: Radiation networks
children.description: Students solve enclosure exchange problems.

topics.title: Heat Exchangers
topics.description: Heat exchangers are the main process-equipment application of heat-transfer theory. Students learn to size, rate, and troubleshoot exchangers for real process streams.

children.title: Heat-exchanger types
children.description: Students recognize common equipment and flow arrangements.

children.title: Double-pipe, shell-and-tube, compact, and plate exchangers
LMTD method
children.description: Students learn the classic design equation for specified inlet/outlet states.

children.title: Effectiveness-NTU method
children.description: Students learn rating methods when outlet temperatures are unknown.

children.title: Design realities
children.description: Students connect clean calculations to industrial equipment.

children.title: Pressure drop, materials, and safety margins

topics.title: Mass Transfer Fundamentals and Diffusion
topics.description: Mass transfer begins with species movement due to concentration gradients. Students learn the analogies and differences between heat diffusion and molecular diffusion.

children.title: Concentration measures
children.description: Students learn how to express species amounts consistently.

children.title: Fick's law
children.description: Students learn the basic flux law for molecular diffusion.

children.title: Diffusion with reaction or generation
children.description: Students model transport coupled to consumption or production.

children.title: Catalyst pellets as an introductory case
Transient diffusion
children.description: Students learn how concentration fields evolve in time.

topics.title: Convective Mass Transfer
topics.description: Convective mass transfer adds fluid motion to diffusion. Students learn how mass-transfer coefficients and dimensionless correlations convert complex flow fields into usable design equations.

children.title: Mass-transfer coefficients
children.description: Students learn the species-transfer counterpart to heat-transfer coefficients.

children.title: Dimensionless mass-transfer groups
children.description: Students use correlations across systems.

children.title: Heat-mass transfer analogies
children.description: Students connect thermal and concentration boundary layers.

children.title: Applications
children.description: Students apply convective mass transfer to equipment and processes.

topics.title: Interphase Mass Transfer
topics.description: Many chemical engineering operations depend on transfer across phase boundaries. Students learn how equilibrium and transport resistances combine at gas-liquid, liquid-liquid, solid-fluid, and membrane interfaces.

children.title: Phase equilibrium
children.description: Students learn the thermodynamic target for interphase transfer.

children.title: Two-film theory
children.description: Students model resistance on both sides of an interface.

children.title: Interfacial area
children.description: Students learn why equipment geometry matters.

children.title: Process examples
children.description: Students connect interphase transfer to separations.

topics.title: Simultaneous Heat and Mass Transfer
topics.description: Real processes often move heat and species at the same time. Students learn to solve coupled balances where temperature affects vapor pressure, diffusivity, equilibrium, and driving forces.

children.title: Coupled balances
children.description: Students learn to write linked energy and species equations.

children.title: Humidification and psychrometrics
children.description: Students analyze air-water vapor systems.

children.title: Drying and evaporation
children.description: Students study common industrial and environmental operations.

children.title: Design and performance evaluation
children.description: Students integrate the course into engineering decisions.
